title: The PCI configuration ports and registers
covers: PCI configuration mechanism 1: the address port at 0CF8h, the data port at 0CFCh, the 64-byte header of configuration space and the device-specific registers that DOSBox-X's emulated VGA and Voodoo cards add, as Ralf Brown's list gives them

rows.text: Port 0CF8h is the 32-bit configuration address port of PCI mechanism 1, written only, beside the data port at 0CFCh.
A write loads the address: bus in bits 23-16, device in 15-11, function in 10-8 and register number in 7-2; bits 30-24 and 1-0 are reserved.
Bit 31 set enables configuration space mapping, and the registers are DWORDs addressed by bits 7-2.
InitializePCI installs write_pci_addr and read_pci_addr at 0CF8h as DWORD handlers.
The address port is readable: a read returns the last value written to it.
0CFCh is the DWORD configuration data port, reached when bit 31 of the address port is set.
A read of the data port returns the configuration data the address port selects.
A write of the data port stores into the configuration data the address port selects.
InitializePCI installs write_pci and read_pci at 0CFCh to 0CFFh, with byte, word and DWORD widths.
A read with bit 31 clear or of an empty bus, device or slot returns all ones; a write to an empty slot is dropped.
The first word of configuration space is the vendor ID, read-only; FFFFh answers when no device exists.
The list gives vendor ID 121Ah to 3DFX Interactive and 5333h to S3.
The vendor ID is read as a word at 00h.
DOSBox-X stores 121Ah for the Voodoo, 5333h for the S3 card and D05Bh for its own VGA.
The second word of configuration space is the device ID, read-only.
The device ID is read as a word at 02h.
DOSBox-X stores 6845h for its own VGA, 8811h for the S3 card by default and 0001h or 0002h for the Voodoo.
The command register is a word at 04h; bits 0 and 1 enable I/O and memory access and bit 2 bus mastering.
Bits 3 to 5 enable special cycle, memory write and invalidate and VGA palette snoop; bits 6 and 7 parity error response and wait cycles.
Bit 8 enables system error and bit 9 fast back-to-back transactions; bits 15-10 are reserved.
The command register is written as a word at 04h of the configuration header.
The word is stored under a write mask: 0403h in the base device, 0023h for both VGA classes and 0123h for the Voodoo.
A new device holds 0023h in the command register for the VGA classes and 0002h for the Voodoo.
The status register is the word at 06h.
Bits 3-0 are reserved; bit 4 says a capabilities list is present.
Bit 5 reports 66 MHz capability and bit 6 UDF support.
Bit 7 reports fast back-to-back capability, bit 8 a data parity error and bits 10-9 the device select timing.
Bits 11 to 14 report target aborts, a master abort and system error, and bit 15 a detected parity error.
Bits 12, 13 and 15 are cleared by writing a 1.
The status register is read as a word at 06h.
A new device holds 0280h in the status word for the VGA classes and 0080h for the Voodoo.
The byte at 08h is the revision ID.
The revision ID is read as a byte at 08h.
DOSBox-X stores 00h for its VGA and most S3 cards, 40h for the Trio64V+ and 02h for the Voodoo.
The three bytes at 09h are the class code: programming interface in bits 7-0, sub-class in 15-8 and class in 23-16.
The class code is read as its three bytes at 09h to 0Bh.
DOSBox-X stores 030000h for its VGA and the S3 card and 040000h for the Voodoo.
The byte at 0Ch is the cache line size.
The cache line size is read as a byte at 0Ch.
DOSBox-X stores 00h in the cache line size on both VGA classes.
The byte at 0Dh is the latency timer.
The latency timer is read as a byte at 0Dh.
DOSBox-X stores 00h in the latency timer on both VGA classes.
The header format is bits 6-0: 00h other, 01h a PCI-to-PCI bridge and 02h a CardBus bridge.
Bit 7 marks a multi-function device.
The header type is read as a byte at 0Eh.
Every emulated card stores 00h, the other header format.
The DWORD at 10h is base address 0, in memory or I/O space as its bit 0 says.
In memory space bits 2-1 place the address anywhere in 4GB, below 1MB or in 64-bit space, and bit 3 is prefetchable.
Bits 31-4 are the base memory address, or 63-4 in 64-bit space; in I/O space bits 31-2 are the base port.
Base address 0 is read as a DWORD at 10h.
DOSBox-X stores the linear frame buffer base with bit 3 set, a prefetchable memory BAR.
The BAR's low bits are reserved by alignment: 8MB on the 86C928, Vision864/964 and Trio32/64, 64MB on the Vision868/968, Trio64V+ and ViRGE/VX, and 16MB on the Voodoo.
A write to the Voodoo's BAR recomputes the LFB address from the new masked value.
DOSBox's own VGA reserves the bits its video memory size needs.
The byte at 3Ch is the interrupt line: 00h none, 01h IRQ1 to 0Fh IRQ15.
The interrupt line is read as a byte at 3Ch.
DOSBox-X stores FFh, outside the document's 00h to 0Fh encoding, commented no irq, on the VGA, S3 and Voodoo cards.
Registers 40h to FFh are 48 DWORDs whose meaning varies by device.
A read of a register in this area returns data whose meaning varies by device.
A guest write of 40h is masked out of the stored byte, which stays 00h, but its low three bits reach VOODOO_PCI_InitEnable.
Registers 40h to FFh are 48 DWORDs whose meaning varies by device.
A read of a register in this area returns data whose meaning varies by device.
The Voodoo2 stores 40h, 01h and 00h at 41h to 43h, a revision ID.
Registers 40h to FFh are 48 DWORDs whose meaning varies by device.
A read of a register in this area returns data whose meaning varies by device.
A read of 4Ch logs a debug line and returns the stored byte.
Registers 40h to FFh are 48 DWORDs whose meaning varies by device.
A read of a register in this area returns data whose meaning varies by device.
A read of 4Dh, 4Eh or 4Fh logs the register number as SST ParseReadRegister STATUS and returns the stored byte.
Registers 40h to FFh are 48 DWORDs whose meaning varies by device.
A read of a register in this area returns data whose meaning varies by device.
On a device with ID 2 or more, 54h to 57h return the bytes of a counter: oscillator_ctr in bits 0-15, the low 12 bits of pci_ctr in 16-27.
On a device with ID 2 or more, reading 54h increments oscillator_ctr and decrements pci_ctr before returning.

A guest write of C0h calls VOODOO_PCI_Enable(true).
